Whitepaper: One Player, Many Signals

Fragmented profiling is quietly costing operators up to 10% of profit

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:05
Instaread

Marketing, risk, and responsible gaming each profile the same player — separately, and rarely reconciled. Our new whitepaper makes the case for one unified profiling layer instead of siloed department controls, and shows what it recovers: reading a player's value and risk within days, keeping bonus spend off abusers, and turning responsible gaming into a driver of retention. Sportradar estimates fragmentation costs operators up to 10% of profit.

Get the whitepaper

Three teams. Three views. One player caught in between

In most operations, profiling happens three times over. Marketing profiles to find players worth targeting. Risk profiles to find the right treatment. Responsible gaming profiles to find players worth protecting. Three separate reads of the same person — rarely reconciled, often contradictory.

So the same customer gets nurtured by one department and restricted by another. Bonuses reach players who exploit them; stake limits hit players who deserve headroom; harm signals surface only once the damage is done. None of it is visible from inside a single function — which is exactly why it goes unseen, and unfixed.
